And the Arabs took Damietta back again,
and the labor of the Franks came to naught.
For before help came to al-Malik al-Kamil,
he repeatedly sent to the Franks and urged them to make peace,
and [offered] to give them Jerusalem, Ascalon, Tiberias, Sidon, Jebail, and Laodicea,
provided only that they would leave Damietta and depart,
so that Egypt and all the country of Egypt would be relieved of them.
The Franks, however, were obstinate,
and demanded also the fortress of al-Karak, and three hundred thousand dinars for the restoration of the walls of Jerusalem which al-Kamil had destroyed.
And because of this al-Kamil was grieved,
and he sent and summoned to his aid his brothers and his co-religionists,
and they took Damietta back from them for nothing.
And the Templars {OCR: Dawwaye} also lost half the revenues of the district of Homs which they used to receive from the Arabs,
and the Hospitallers {OCR?} the tribute which they had on Ba'rin.
Now Damietta remained with the Franks on this occasion for one year, ten months, and twenty-four days.
And at this time,
the Ismailis jumped upon Sir Adam, the regent of the kingdom of the Armenians,
in a narrow path that descends opposite our church of Mar Bar Sawma in the city of Sis,
and they killed him.
And in his place arose as regent Baron Constantine, son of Baron Basil, the uncle of King Leo.
Now when Raymond-Roupen heard that King Leo had already died,
and that also the regent of the kingdom, that Sir Adam, had also been killed,
he arose, took his mother, the daughter of King Roupen the Great, and traveled by sea.
And he arrived at the port of the fortress of Corycus,
in order to enter and reign in Cilicia.
The lord of this fortress, however,
who was Baron Bahram, the lord of Sarvandikar,
did not give him leave to cross,
but even threatened him,
that if he did not give him his mother as a wife,
he would certainly seize him and also destroy him.
